title: feat(spec): BlueprintViewSchema and StrictView declare filters and sort, so an AI-built view carries its own filter
body:
Fixes #24129
Clause-②: yes (widening)

## What

A solution-blueprint view can now carry the filter its name promises. `BlueprintViewSchema` (lenient, what `apply_blueprint` parses) and `StrictView` inside `SolutionBlueprintStrictSchema` (the OpenAI-strict `generateObject` contract the design model generates against) both declare `filters` and `sort`. This is ruling A on objectstack-ai/cloud#2932 (「2932 同意」), as the card restates it; the cloud ruling text is not readable from this session.

Before this, a plan could say 「overdue only」 in a view's name and nowhere else, so the applier shipped an unfiltered grid under that name (objectstack-ai/cloud#2922). Neither key invents a format.

### `filters`: which records the view shows, ANDed

| | Lenient `BlueprintViewSchema.filters` | Strict `StrictView.filters` |
|:--|:--|:--|
| presence | optional | required, nullable (null = a view over every record) |
| element | `ViewFilterRuleSchema` itself (identity-pinned in the test) | inline `StrictViewFilterRule`, keys pinned equal to `ViewFilterRuleSchema`'s |
| `field` | `string` | `string` (no `SNAKE_CASE` on either side: value parity) |
| `operator` | `z.preprocess(fold, z.enum(VIEW_FILTER_OPERATORS))`: canonical, legacy spellings folded | `z.enum(VIEW_FILTER_OPERATORS)`: canonical only, no fold |
| `value` | optional; string, number, boolean, null, or a list of strings or numbers | required, nullable; string, number, boolean, or a list of strings or numbers |
| operator/value shape (`in` takes an array, `between` takes `[min, max]`, `icontains` takes a non-empty string) | refused by the reused refinement | not expressed |

Why each strict-side difference exists:
- **`value` nullable, not optional.** Strict mode needs every key listed in `required`, and null is how this mirror spells "optional". It is also the spelling the unary operators use. The blueprint tools strip nulls before the lenient parse, so the lenient rule sees `value` absent, which it accepts for unary operators.
- **No fold on `operator`.** The lenient `z.preprocess` is a parse-time transform with no JSON-Schema form. A model emitting the canonical vocabulary is the alias table's own contract for new producers. The strict test pins that `eq` is refused at `views.0.filters.0.operator` with `invalid_value`.
- **No operator/value-shape refinement.** A refinement has no JSON-Schema form, and the strict mirror precedent already leaves out what strict mode cannot express (`questions.max(2)`, `seedData`). The lenient parse that `apply_blueprint` runs refuses these, and a test pins it (`in` with a scalar, issue at `views.0.filters.0.value`, code `custom`). The describe on the strict `value` states the shape rules for the model.

### `sort`: default record order

| | Lenient | Strict |
|:--|:--|:--|
| presence | optional | required, nullable (null = the platform default order) |
| element | the shared `SortItemSchema` (`shared/enums.zod.ts`, identity-pinned) | inline `{ field: string, order: SortDirectionEnum }`, both keys required |
| form | array only; a `"field desc"` string is refused (`invalid_type` at `views.0.sort`) | array only |

`ListView.sort`'s entry is an inline `strictObject` and is not exported. `SortItemSchema` is the exported shared sort item, and that entry's own comment says its titles mirror it: the same `{ field, order }` keys and the same `asc` / `desc` vocabulary. The two differ in one way. The `ListView` entry rejects unknown keys and folds `direction` to `order`. `SortItemSchema` is a plain `z.object`, so it strips unknown keys, which is the posture of every other blueprint shape. A `{ field, direction }` entry is still refused: `order` is required and has no default, so it cannot silently reverse a sort. The blueprint does not accept a string form, because `ListView.sort` no longer does.

### Describes

Both sides tell the model that a view whose name or label states a condition (「overdue / 逾期」, 「my open / 我的未完成」, 「待审批」, 「本月」) MUST carry the rules that make the name true. They give worked rules that use the platform's declared tokens `{today}` (date macros) and `{current_user_id}` (context tokens). Both tokens are expanded on both sides of the wire, and `examples/app-todo`'s overdue list view uses the same rule pair. The describe prose is deliberately not pinned by a test.

## Tests (`packages/spec/src/ai/solution-blueprint.test.ts`)

- Lenient: carries `filters` and `sort` through the parse; both optional; identity pins (`filters` element `toBe(ViewFilterRuleSchema)`, `sort` element `toBe(SortItemSchema)`); a bad operator is refused at `views.0.filters.0.operator` (`invalid_value`); `in` with a scalar at `views.0.filters.0.value` (`custom`); a bad `order` at `views.0.sort.0.order` (`invalid_value`); a string sort at `views.0.sort` (`invalid_type`).
- Strict: carries rules, including `in` with a list and `is_null` with null; null accepted for both keys; each key is required (omitting it gives `invalid_type` at that key); a rule's `value` key is required (`invalid_union`); `eq` is refused; a bad `order` is refused. The existing gallery/gantt strict fixture now sends `filters: null, sort: null`.
- Key parity, extended a level further out (fields, then objects, then nav items, now VIEWS): the view key sets are equal, with no deliberate exclusions. The nested filter-rule and sort-entry key sets are equal. The strict operator enum equals the lenient one, and the strict `order` enum equals the lenient one. The VALUE-parity walker covers the new string leaves automatically: `views[].filters[].field` and `views[].sort[].field` carry no pattern on either side.

## Generated and ledger artifacts

- Regenerated by the generators: `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json` (+`BlueprintView:filters`, +`BlueprintView:sort`), `content/docs/references/ai/solution-blueprint.mdx`, `docs/audits/2026-07-unknown-key-strictness-ledger.counts/ai.md` (ai sites 78 to 80: the two inline strict shapes), and `skills/objectstack-ai/references/_index.md` (see below). `api-surface/`, `json-schema.manifest/`, `declaration-map/`, `export-origins/` and `authorable-surface.base.json` did not move, because there are no new exports.
- **Hand-edited ledger, as `build-schemas.ts` requires:** `packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json` gains `ai/BlueprintView: ["filters.element"]` and `views.element.filters.element` on `ai/SolutionBlueprint` (sites 764 to 766, schemas 234 to 235). This is the `ViewFilterRuleSchema` refinement that the published lenient JSON Schema cannot carry. `ui/ListView` already declares the same gap as `filter.element`. The strict schema carries no refinement and drops nothing.
- **The published strict JSON Schema** (`json-schema/ai/SolutionBlueprintStrict.json`, built locally): `views.items.required` is now `object, name, label, type, columns, groupBy, filters, sort`, with `additionalProperties: false`. The rule item requires `field, operator, value`, and `operator` is the 20-member canonical enum. The sort item requires `field, order`, and `order` is the enum `asc, desc`.

### `skills/**`: one generator-owned file moves

`gen:skill-refs` lists each skill's transitive spec modules. The blueprint now imports `ui/view.zod` and `shared/enums.zod`, so `skills/objectstack-ai/references/_index.md` gains 7 pointer lines (`shared/enums.zod`, `shared/http.zod`, and `ui/view.zod` with its `bulk-action`, `chart`, `i18n` and `sharing` modules). Without it, the required `check:skill-refs` is red.
- Readings: the changed file goes from 43 to 50 lines. The whole published skill package (the sum of all `skills/*/SKILL.md`) goes from 4389 to 4389 lines: no SKILL.md is touched.
- Governance, `node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --branch claude/issue-24129-blueprint-view-filters-sort` on head `d896c66e6`: "governed-surface predicate: 0 of 8 path(s) hit the register after 1 generated-artifact lift(s) (7 surfaces govern objectstack). ✅ NOT governed — ordinary queue landing applies to a PR with exactly this file list." The index is a PURE REGENERATION, byte-equal to `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec gen:skill-refs` recomputed on this tree. That is the generator-owned carve-out in that script, and `governed-surface-guard.yml` installs the toolchain so the queue guard can recompute the same answer. No hand-authored `skills/**` content moves. Size: 325 changed lines (+318 / -7), under the 3000 threshold.

## Local verification

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build`: exit 0. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run --project local --maxWorkers=2`: 692 files, 20969 passed, 1 todo, exit 0. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck`: exit 0. These ran at `0b87a3245`. The later merge of `origin/main` (`d896c66e6`) brings only `docs/qa/**` and `examples/app-showcase/**`, so no spec input moved.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated`: "✓ All 14 generated artifacts are up to date", on `d896c66e6`.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derived 113 commands, and all 113 ran on `d896c66e6` with exit 0. `--ran` reconciliation: "113 derived, 113 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN". On the first pass (at `0b87a3245`), seven gates refused with exit 3 because a prerequisite was unbuilt or a fixture commit was not in the shallow clone. They were re-run green after `turbo run build` of formula, lint, client, client-react and objectql, and a depth-1 fetch of the fixture commit.
- `pnpm check:dev-prereqs` (local-only family): exit 0.
- Not run locally, left to CI: the `test:repo` project, the integration tiers, and the path-scheduled CI jobs `dispatch-gates` lists (Test Core shards, Build Core, Build Docs, dogfood).

## Acceptance notes

- **Key name.** The blueprint key is `filters`, as the ruling and the card name it. The runtime `ListView` key is `filter`. The applier (cloud, not readable here) is what expands a blueprint view into a `ListView` body, so the mapping between the two spellings lives there. The lenient blueprint schemas are `z.object`s and strip undeclared keys, so a hand-authored blueprint view that writes the singular `filter` loses it silently. The same is true of every other undeclared blueprint key, and the strict path cannot emit an undeclared key at all.
- **The strict mirror's own accept set narrows.** A strict document without `filters` / `sort` on a view parsed before and is refused now. That holds for every key ever added to this mirror (`viewName`, `nameField`, `sharingModel`, `expression` all shipped the same required-nullable way, under Minor Changes). The mirror is a generation contract, so its only producer is the model, which receives the new JSON Schema. It is declared `Clause-②: yes (widening)` as the card rules. The contract review may weigh this.
- **In-repo consumers** (`git grep` on this head, outside `packages/spec`): only a comment in `packages/cli/src/lint/metadata-eval.ts` (the type name `SolutionBlueprint`), plus the generated docs. The real producer and consumer are cloud's `propose_blueprint` / `apply_blueprint`. Its interim `.extend()` (cloud PR #2931) is not readable here, and its key spelling was not compared.
- **Surface beyond the claim's file list**, all mechanically required: the dropped-refinements ledger lines, the strictness-ledger count shard, and the skill index regeneration.
